reasons.D: Long, and-joined advisory sentences and a businesslike working of the investment figure ('you had better see that he is the kind of security which will pay a return') come closest to the passage's plain, practical, slightly period voice; the closing quip is a little more polished than the author.
reasons.C: Plain, direct stance and practical advice ('I owe you a plain answer') fit the author's frankness, but the diction and colon-led lists read modern and the rhythm is tighter than the passage's loose accumulation.
reasons.B: 'Now consider' and the friendly tone echo the author, but the stream of short epigrammatic sentences ('He drops his hat, and it is only a hat') is a literary wit the passage does not show.
reasons.A: The most formal and essayistic, with balanced aphorisms and elevated diction ('lavish your best observation', 'earn their keep'); none of the author's homely, colloquial looseness.
